sections.h2: How do you sell a house fast in Bullhead City, AZ?
sections.html:
Choose between listing with an agent, selling it yourself, or accepting a cash offer, and match the choice to how soon you need the money. The condition of the house and the clarity of the title shape the timeline more than the route does.

The Census Bureau estimates 43,987 residents as of July 1, 2025. Owners occupy 69.9 percent of housing, the median home value is $211,500, and 34.3 percent of residents are 65 or older. Median household income is $50,556 and 18.7 percent of residents live in poverty.

  • Pull the parcel number and tax bill from the Mohave County Treasurer before you talk to buyers.
  • Decide in advance whether you will repair, credit the buyer or sell as-is.
  • Ask each buyer for a closing date and a written list of seller costs.

sections.h2: Where is Bullhead City and how did it grow?
sections.html:
Bullhead City sits on the Arizona side of the Colorado River in western Mohave County, directly across from Laughlin, Nevada. Las Vegas is 97 miles north, Kingman is 34 miles east, Needles, California is 22 miles south, and Phoenix is 216 miles southeast. The city covers about 60 square miles at 925 feet of elevation and is the largest city in Mohave County by land area. It sits at the southern end of Lake Mohave.

The Mojave people were the earliest residents. In 1864 the site hosted Hardyville, a ferry, steamboat landing and toll road settlement that faded after the railroads bypassed it. The modern town grew from construction of Davis Dam between 1942 and 1953, first called Bullhead Dam for a rock formation the rising water later covered. In 1984 the communities of Bullhead City, Riviera and Holiday Shores voted to incorporate under the Bullhead City name. Population has moved from 21,951 in 1990 to 33,769 in 2000, 39,540 in 2010 and 41,348 in 2020.

Casinos and tourism around Laughlin supply much of the employment. Water recreation fills the summer, and winter brings visitors in motor homes from colder states.

sections.h2: What roads, schools and parks matter to Bullhead City buyers?
sections.html:
State Routes 95 and 68 are the local highways, and Interstate 40 is reached through Needles or Kingman. The Bullhead Area Transit System runs the public bus network, and Greyhound and TUFESA serve the city. Laughlin/Bullhead International Airport is the largest airport in Mohave County, but no scheduled commercial flights operate there at present.

Elementary and junior high schools belong to the Bullhead City School District, with Sunrise, Coyote Canyon, Desert Valley and Diamondback elementary schools, Bullhead City Middle School and Fox Creek Junior High. Mohave High School and River Valley High School are run by the Colorado River Union High School District. Mohave Community College and a Northern Arizona University campus are in the city.

Rotary Park is the biggest city park at 300 acres of riverfront with beaches, a boat ramp, a dog park and a disc golf course. Ken Fovargue Park has ball fields and a public pool. The annual river regatta and the winter sports tournaments are the area's best-known events.

The Mohave County Library branch in Bullhead City was remodeled and expanded in 2011 into a 24,000 square foot building. The Hardyville Pioneer Cemetery, a small historic landmark, is the main surviving remnant of the 1860s settlement.

sections.h2: How do Mohave County property taxes work when you sell in Bullhead City?
sections.html:
The Mohave County Treasurer bills property taxes, with bills mailed by the first of October. Taxes are due October 1 and, for most property, can be paid in two installments. The first installment is past due after 5 pm on November 1, and the second is due March 1 and past due after 5 pm on May 1. Taxes of $100 or less are due in full October 1 and become past due after December 31. Paying both installments by December 31 removes interest accrued after November 1. If a date falls on a weekend or holiday, the deadline moves to 5 pm the next business day, which applies to November 1, 2026, a Sunday.

Late payment carries an annual 16 percent penalty, prorated monthly. The county notes the Treasurer is not required to mail a bill and taxes are due even if you never receive one. If you sold the property and still receive a bill, forward it to the buyer or return it to the Treasurer at P.O. Box 712, Kingman, AZ 86402 with the new owner's name. A drop box for payments is at 1130 Hancock Road in Bullhead City, and cash is accepted only at the main office in Kingman.

sections.h2: Which tax relief programs might affect a Mohave County buyer or seller?
sections.html:
Mohave County's Assessor runs exemptions for widows, widowers, disabled civilians and disabled veterans. For tax year 2026, the total allowable exemption was $4,873 of assessed limited property value, the combined Arizona property could not exceed $36,454 in assessed value, and qualifying income could not exceed $39,865 per household, or $47,826 with minor children at home. Applications ran January 2 through February 28, 2026, and enrollment reopens in January 2027.

State Aid to Education also reduces the primary school tax on owner-occupied homes. A mobile home that is not affixed to the land can generate two tax notices, one for the land and one for the home, so a buyer of a mobile home should ask the Assessor whether it has been affixed. Whether a buyer qualifies for any of this depends on their own situation, and the county Assessor makes that call.

sections.h2: What are the recording and permit steps for a Bullhead City sale?
sections.html:
Ownership changes on the tax roll only when a deed is recorded with the Mohave County Recorder, which sends the information to the Assessor. The Recorder's posted fee is $30 for most documents, $3 for certification and $1 per page for copies, and checks are made payable to the Mohave County Recorder. The state's sales affidavit rules apply: an Affidavit of Property Value must accompany the transfer unless an A.R.S. 11-1134 exemption code is noted on the deed, and the date of sale is the contract date.

For permits, ask Bullhead City's building and zoning staff whether work done on your house was permitted. If you plan to repair before listing, confirm with the city what needs a permit before a contractor starts.

faqs.q: When are Mohave County property taxes due?
faqs.a: They are due October 1. The first installment is past due after 5 pm on November 1, and the second is due March 1 and past due after May 1. Taxes of $100 or less are past due after December 31.

faqs.q: What is the median home value in Bullhead City?
faqs.a: The Census Bureau reports $211,500 for owner-occupied homes from 2020 to 2024, with median gross rent of $1,079.

faqs.q: Where do I send a tax bill for a house I already sold?
faqs.a: Forward it to the new owner, or return it to the Mohave County Treasurer at P.O. Box 712, Kingman, AZ 86402 with the owner's name and date of sale.

faqs.q: How much does Mohave County charge to record a deed?
faqs.a: The Recorder lists $30 for all documents unless otherwise specified. Copies are $1 per page and certified copies add $3 per document.

faqs.q: Which school districts serve Bullhead City?
faqs.a: The Bullhead City School District runs elementary and junior high schools, and the Colorado River Union High School District runs Mohave High School and River Valley High School.
